title: Reconcile the mbpm2 output-contract report: schemaVersion cannot select a decoder, but the relayed shape does not reproduce here (OPAG-142)
description:
Filed 2026-09-17 to satisfy OPAG-142 fourth acceptance criterion, which requires the mbpm2 output-contract item to exist as a quest-cli task rather than only as a record in opum-agent OPAG-140.

RELAYED CLAIM, via opum-agent, one clause and not the original report: "both envelope shapes report schemaVersion 1, so a consumer cannot select a decoder".

WHAT WAS MEASURED HERE, against quest 0.7.1 as installed (/Users/jdnewhouse/.nvm/versions/node/v24.20.0/bin/quest), before filing:

  success, task list   {schemaVersion:1, contractVersion:1, kind:"task.list", data:array}
  success, task view   {schemaVersion:1, contractVersion:1, kind:"task.view", data:object}
  error, not_found     keys exactly [error_type, message, principal] -- NO schemaVersion, NO contractVersion
  error, usage         keys exactly [error_type, message, principal] -- NO schemaVersion, NO contractVersion

So the relayed sentence does not reproduce for success-versus-error: the error envelope reports no schemaVersion at all, and a consumer can discriminate the two trivially, by presence of schemaVersion or kind, or by error_type. This repository CLAUDE.md profile already records the same asymmetry from the other direction -- contractVersion went on success envelopes only, and both error paths carry none.

WHAT IS TRUE AND MAY BE THE REAL POINT: schemaVersion is a CONSTANT. It is 1 on every success envelope of every kind, and it has never varied. It therefore carries no selection information, and the field that actually discriminates payload shape is kind -- task.list returns an array, task.view returns an object, both under schemaVersion 1. A consumer who believed schemaVersion was the decoder selector would indeed be unable to select one, which is a defensible reading of the report and a legitimate contract observation. But it is a different statement from the relayed one, and it is about two SUCCESS shapes rather than "both envelope shapes".

DO NOT IMPLEMENT FROM THIS TASK AS WRITTEN. The first step is to obtain mbpm2 original report through opum-agent and establish which object was measured -- a different CLI or surface, an older quest build, or the constant-schemaVersion reading above. Naming the object measured and the object the claim is about, and confirming they are the same one, is this repository own standing rule and is exactly what one relayed clause cannot carry.

Filed with the discrepancy recorded rather than resolved, because filing a transcription of a claim that does not reproduce would put a wrong fact in the tracker, and a wrong fact recorded as a task is harder to dislodge than an open question.

acceptanceCriteria.text: mbpm2 original report is obtained and the object it measured is identified -- which binary, which command family, which envelope pair -- rather than reasoning from the one-clause relay

The discrepancy is resolved one way or the other: either the relayed claim reproduces against some object and that object is named, or it is withdrawn as a relay artifact and mbpm2 plus opum-agent are told

If a real defect survives that reconciliation, it is stated as its own acceptance criteria -- whether schemaVersion should ever vary, whether kind is the documented decoder selector, and whether the error envelope should carry schemaVersion at all -- rather than being inherited from this tasks framing
Whatever is concluded is reflected back to OPAG-142/OPAG-140 so the fleet record and this one do not diverge

implementationNotes:
CANDIDATE ANSWER to acceptance criterion 1, supplied by opum-agent 2026-09-17 and recorded before it is confirmed: the version gap may resolve this on its own, making both claims correct and neither transferable.

mbpm2 measured the published 0.6.2 PAIR. This session measured 0.7.1 as installed. Two different byte-sets, and the envelope may simply have changed between them -- notably, contractVersion did not exist before 0.7.0 (QCLI-289), so the 0.6.2 success envelope was a different shape from the one measured here. If the error envelope also differed at 0.6.2, "both envelope shapes report schemaVersion 1" could have been exactly true then and exactly false now, with no defect on either side and nothing to fix beyond the relay.

Check this FIRST, before treating the discrepancy as substantive. It is cheap: read the 0.6.2 envelopes, not the current ones.

PROVENANCE of the relayed clause, volunteered by opum-agent against their own relay: it reached them through OPAG-140, which is itself a FILING RECORD of something mbpm2 reported -- they never read the measurement, they relayed a sentence. They named this as the fleet "a filing record is not the measurement" rule failing on the exact subject it governs, and as the second instance in three days of a figure reaching a repository by relay rather than by reading.

The original lives on host mbpm2 at results/analysis/proof-graph-pilot-20260913/build-validation/lore-quest-0.6.2-20260914/validation-report.md. Every mbpm2 session was offline, so the user is the only bridge; opum-agent has added a request for the RAW report, plus which quest build was measured, to a handover prompt already with the user. Do not start work on this task until that lands.

INDEPENDENT of whatever comes back: the unwrapped reading stands on its own. schemaVersion is a constant, has never varied, therefore carries no selection information, and kind is the field that actually discriminates payload shape. opum-agent framing, worth keeping verbatim: a version field that cannot vary is a signal that reports "unchanged" because it is incapable of reporting anything else. That is worth fixing whether or not it is what mbpm2 hit, and it should not be dropped if the relay turns out to be a version artifact.

opum-agent confirmed 2026-09-17T17:56Z: the relayed claim ("both envelope shapes report schemaVersion 1") was never measured on their end, only relayed, and they now endorse the version-gap hypothesis this task already recorded as the one to test first. Blocker status is now precise: TASK-61-style rationale would need a live mbpm2 session (all offline, cannot be fetched), but this task needs only a DOCUMENT at a known path (results/analysis/proof-graph-pilot-20260913/build-validation/lore-quest-0.6.2-20260914/validation-report.md) on a host confirmed reachable over the mesh at 13:43Z 2026-09-17. Recorded on OPAG-142 as the next orchestrators first action -- fetching that file and checking whether the 0.6.2 error envelope carried schemaVersion 1 is the concrete next step, not further investigation here.

RESOLVED 2026-09-17T18:05Z, via opum-agent fetching the actual mbpm2 report and this session independently verifying it over SSH (~/.scripts/mbpm2) rather than trusting the relay: wc -c matched the claimed 7816 bytes exactly, and grep -n for "schemaVersion|contractVersion|decoder" returned zero hits (exit 1) -- the word schemaVersion does not appear anywhere in the source document. The quoted passages opum-agent relayed were checked verbatim against the file and match at the exact line numbers cited (lines 37-38 and 60-62).

CONCLUSION: the relayed claim ("both envelope shapes report schemaVersion 1, so a consumer cannot select a decoder") was never in mbpm2s original report. It was manufactured somewhere in the OPAG-140 -> OPAG-142 relay chain, plausibly as a rendering of "the consumer had no way to tell the shape changed" into a specific, wrong, and unverified technical claim about a field. There is nothing to reproduce because there was never anything reported in those terms. My own version-gap hypothesis (that it was true at 0.6.2 and superseded by QCLI-289) is therefore moot -- not confirmed, not refuted, just never the right question.

WHAT MBPM2 ACTUALLY REPORTED, quoted directly: quest 0.6.2s changelog "explicitly calls its normalized mutation envelopes a breaking change (QCLI-264/QCLI-265), despite the patch version" -- data.task became bare data, correctly and deliberately, but shipped under a 0.6.x PATCH bump with no version-number signal that anything could break. This is a real, different, and already-historical defect: a SemVer-discipline gap, not a decoder-selection one. Filed separately as QCLI-328 (new scope per this repository own task-execution rule -- work discovered outside a tasks acceptance criteria is a new task, not folded into this one).

AC3s original framing (whether schemaVersion should ever vary, whether kind is the documented decoder selector, whether the error envelope should carry schemaVersion) is DECLINED rather than pursued further: kind already reliably discriminates payload shape today (task.list -> array, task.view -> object), and contractVersion (QCLI-289) already exists as the forward-looking mechanism for signaling envelope-shape changes -- making schemaVersion itself vary now would be the higher-blast-radius fix QCLI-289s own notes already weighed against (opum-cli-e2e hardcodes schemaVersion==1 across ~41 call sites) for no consumer-facing gap that contractVersion does not already close. No further action taken on that question.

AC4 (reflect back to OPAG-142/OPAG-140): done via direct message to opum-agent recording this resolution; they confirmed their successor will land it on OPAG-142.
finalSummary: The relayed claim ("both envelope shapes report schemaVersion 1, so a consumer cannot select a decoder") does not describe anything mbpm2 actually reported. Independently verified over SSH against the source document on host mbpm2 (byte count and grep both confirm): the word schemaVersion appears zero times in the report. It was fabricated somewhere in the OPAG-140->OPAG-142 relay chain. What mbpm2 actually reported is real and different: quest 0.6.2 shipped the QCLI-264/QCLI-265 data.task->data breaking change under a PATCH version bump, with no version-number signal that anything could break -- a SemVer-discipline gap, filed separately as QCLI-328. The schemaVersion-is-a-constant observation this task also surfaced (kind is the actual shape discriminator, not schemaVersion) is declined rather than pursued: contractVersion (QCLI-289) already closes the consumer-facing gap, and varying schemaVersion itself would be the higher-blast-radius fix that task already weighed against.
